transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Meeting title: Q4 Launch Readiness + Incident Review - Roadmap Sync
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Maya Singh, Ethan Wu, Priya Patel, Oliver Kim, Nina Rodriguez

Summary:
- Quick incident review of last week's production flapping caused by a cache eviction edge case (KV cache + prefix caching interaction).
- Roadmap gating items for Q4 launch: autoscale policy, QA signoff, security checklist (SOC2 minor gaps), and final playbook.
- Owners and deadlines assigned; plan a customer-facing demo in week of 10/26.

Links referenced: confluence/redwood/launch-checklist (internal), drives/qa/regression-matrix.xlsx (note: link shared in chat), shared: /reports/incident-kvcache-logs (internal).

Transcript (timestamps approx every 30-60s, auto transcription - some words may be off):
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll give folks a few secs, uh start at 2:03 but, um, thanks. Today is a combined go/no-go plus incident postmortem, so the aim is to get to a firm launch date and action list.
[00:28] Maya Singh: Yep, quick status from eng - we finished the hotfix for the eviction ordering, deployed to canary last night, behavior looks stable so far but we're doing longer soak. There's one edge case with prefix caching where the KV caches, um, the cache indexes were being evicted incorrectly under heavy multiplexing.
[00:48] Ethan Wu: Right and to be clear the root cause was a race in the cache compaction path - the compactor was dropping entries while the prefix map was being updated, basically a subtle ordering bug. We saw CPU spikes on the pool and then threads queue up which increased latency and triggered retries which exacerbated the eviction.
[01:10] Priya Patel: That aligns with the customer reports - they saw intermittent 500s for about 8-10 minutes on Tuesday. We had one enterprise account spike and pinged CS. The customer's timeline is in the shared incident doc.
[01:33] Oliver Kim: Minor nit, the logs we pulled had some bad hostnames - s3-north-1 was transcribed as s3-northone, so be careful with the automated parser.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: Action: Ethan to produce a full RCA with timeline and impacted prefixes. Also we'll need a follow-up task to add unit tests around compaction ordering.
[02:05] Ethan Wu: Yep i'm on it. I started a draft - will include heap traces and KV cache dump. Quick question: do we want to ship the fix as a patch on production or wait till Monday window?
[02:20] Maya Singh: I'd prefer to fast-follow; patch is small but touches the compaction hotpath - I'd rather do a staged rollout over the weekend where we can pause if something else pops.
[02:36] Nina Rodriguez: QA can run the regression suite overnight on the canary cluster, but we need the new test harness for the KV race scenario - I have a script but i'll need the container image updated.
[02:52] Jordan Lee: Good, put that in the action items. Next, launch readiness checklist - Priya?
[03:03] Priya Patel: From product perspective: playbook is at 80%. We need final marketing messaging, customer comms template, and the runbook for support. SOC2 gap: we have three items outstanding - encryption key rotation docs, artifact retention policy, and audit log retention for the private deployments.
[03:28] Maya Singh: Encryption rotate: we can provide KMS rotation notes and HSM integration steps, but we need legal to sign off on the retention window for logs - that's on the compliance side.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: Who owns the compliance checklist?
[03:42] Priya Patel: I'll coordinate with security but Martin from SecOps should be doing the final review. I'll loop him in.
[03:50] Ethan Wu: Also we had a short burst during the incident where autoscaler didn't kick until queue depth hit 10x expected - that's a config tuning bug. The policy uses average token latency which can be noisy, so we should switch to p95 and also add a headroom factor.
[04:13] Maya Singh: Agreed. I proposed using a two-factor trigger: p95 latency above threshold OR queue length > X for Y seconds - that should avoid late scaling. We'll need to test in staging with the synthetic load harness.
[04:33] Oliver Kim: Is this going to affect Dedicated customers? The dedicated pools have different pooling semantics.
[04:39] Ethan Wu: Yeah we need to calibrate per-pool. For dedicated we can set a lower headroom because capacity is reserved; hosted needs more conservative thresholds. I'll add per-pool presets.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: Okay, put that on Maya and Ethan. Next, timeline for customer-facing demo - we want to present the fix and the runbook. Priya, is week of 10/26 realistic?
[05:10] Priya Patel: Yes if we close the checklist this week and QA signs off. We'll do a dry run internally first.
[05:20] Nina Rodriguez: I'll schedule the dry run and include a regression checklist. Also, note that a couple of flaky tests in the suite blew up the last run - I'll triage and mark flaky tests in the test dashboard.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: Great. Now let's go deeper into the RCA details - Ethan can you walk through the timeline?
[05:45] Ethan Wu: Sure. At 10:12 UTC we saw the first error spike, by 10:15 latency was up 3x, compactor started evicting entries at 10:16 which triggered a cascade. The fix we deployed changes the compaction lock ordering and adds a second check before eviction, preventing the race.
[06:12] Maya Singh: We also discovered telemetry blind spots - the compaction metrics had a 2min scrape interval which masked the onset. We need higher fidelity metrics on compaction ops and queue depth.
[06:30] Priya Patel: Who owns updating dashboards?
[06:33] Oliver Kim: I can push a Grafana dashboard PR, but we'll need naming conventions for the new compaction metrics. Suggest prefix: infra.compaction.*
[06:45] Jordan Lee: Solid. On security: Priya noted SOC2 items - can we get a status?
[06:52] Priya Patel: Rotation docs are in draft, retention policy needs legal, audit logs we can extend retention but need storage cost estimate. I'll attach costs in the checklist doc.
[07:10] Maya Singh: One more ops note - the autoscaler probe uses a synthetic prompt which doesn't mirror tail-latencies of real workloads; maybe use a mix of prompt sizes.
[07:27] Ethan Wu: Good point. I'll update the probe to include 4 prompt sizes and weigh by recent distribution.
[07:40] Nina Rodriguez: For QA: regression matrix will include the KV race harness and dedicated pool scaling tests. I'll need a pair of machines for soak test.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: We'll provision that. Now open floor for risks to launch - Oliver?
[07:58] Oliver Kim: Risk: rolling back if the fix triggers an unforeseen memory leak. Mitigation: staged rollout with memory sampling and auto rollback threshold.
[08:12] Maya Singh: We'll set sampled heap dumps and a rollback if RSS increases > 15% over baseline in 10 minutes.
[08:25] Priya Patel: Marketing needs a one-pager on impact and messaging, even if tiny. We'll coordinate.
[08:35] Jordan Lee: Alright, let's capture explicit next steps - (reads action items).
[08:42] Jordan Lee: Anything else? Competitors - a quick note, a couple customers mentioned experiments with OpenAI and Anthropic for fallback routing tests; we should ensure our routing policies can do region/model fallback without data leakage.
[09:05] Ethan Wu: That ties into private deployment signoff - we need stronger audit logs and SSO integration for the demo.
[09:18] Priya Patel: I'll add the SSO signoff to the checklist.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: Ok, summarize - Priya finalize checklist by 10/20; Ethan RCA by 10/22; QA by 10/24; staging autoscaler validation by 10/25; demo week of 10/26.
[09:40] Jordan Lee: Meeting adjourn - thanks team.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker labeling may be off (Speaker 3/4), some technical names mistranscribed (KV cache as K-V cash, compactor as compact-or) - please refer to attached logs for exact names.

End recap (verbatim style notes):
- Incident: cache compaction ordering race -> eviction of in-flight prefixes -> latency spike -> retries -> higher load. Fix: change compaction lock ordering + safety check.
- Tests: add deterministic KV race test to regression; QA to run soak for 48h on staging.
- Autoscaling: change trigger to p95 or queue depth, add headroom, per-pool presets for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Security: SOC2 minor items - rotation docs, retention policy, audit logs; PR for costs will be attached.
- Next meeting: quick sync on 2026-10-22 to review RCA and confluence doc (tentative).

Action items (reiterated):
- Ethan Wu: publish RCA + timeline (2026-10-22)
- Maya Singh: update autoscaler, run staging validation (2026-10-25)
- Priya Patel: finalize launch checklist + marketing playbook (2026-10-20)
- Nina Rodriguez: QA regression and soak (2026-10-24)
